regions.name: Europe
regions.blurb: Most of Europe is covered by the Schengen Area: one short-stay visa policy for 29 countries, with ETIAS pre-travel authorisation being phased in for visa-exempt visitors and the EES biometric entry system now operating at external borders.

regions.name: Central Asia
regions.blurb: Once among the hardest regions to enter, Central Asia has opened up: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan waive visas for many passports, and eVisa portals cover most of the rest. Registration rules after arrival still apply in several countries.

regions.name: East Asia
regions.blurb: Japan, South Korea and Taiwan offer generous visa waivers to many passports, while mainland China combines visa exemptions with a large embassy-visa system. Electronic arrival procedures are standard.

regions.name: Southeast Asia
regions.blurb: Visa policy varies widely across Southeast Asia — from broad visa exemptions in Thailand and Malaysia to eVisa regimes in Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia. Digital arrival cards are increasingly mandatory across the region.

regions.name: South Asia
regions.blurb: India, Sri Lanka and Nepal run large eVisa or on-arrival programmes; requirements vary sharply by nationality, and yellow fever certificates are checked for travellers arriving from risk countries.

regions.name: Middle East
regions.blurb: The Gulf states run modern eVisa and on-arrival systems; Saudi Arabia requires specific vaccinations for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims. Israel entry stamps can affect onward travel in parts of the region.

regions.name: North Africa
regions.blurb: Morocco and Tunisia are visa-free for many Western passports, Egypt sells visas on arrival and online, and Algeria and Libya remain strict embassy-visa countries. Overland borders in the region open and close with little notice.

regions.name: West Africa
regions.blurb: ECOWAS citizens move freely across West Africa, while most other visitors need an eVisa or embassy visa. Yellow fever vaccination certificates are a near-universal entry condition throughout the region.

regions.name: East Africa
regions.blurb: Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Rwanda run eVisa or electronic-authorisation systems, and the East Africa Tourist Visa covers three countries in one. Yellow fever certificates are checked for arrivals from risk countries.

regions.name: Central Africa
regions.blurb: Central Africa remains one of the strictest visa regions: most visitors need an embassy visa arranged in advance, letters of invitation are common, and yellow fever vaccination is mandatory almost everywhere.

regions.name: Southern Africa
regions.blurb: South Africa, Namibia and Botswana waive visas for many passports, and SADC citizens travel freely across much of the region. Blank passport pages and proof of onward travel are checked more often here than almost anywhere else.

regions.name: North & Central America
regions.blurb: The United States (ESTA) and Canada (eTA) require electronic travel authorisation from visa-waiver nationals; Mexico and most of Central America are visa-free for Western passports, with proof of onward travel commonly checked.

regions.name: South America
regions.blurb: Most of South America is visa-free for Western passports, and MERCOSUR citizens travel with ID cards alone. Several countries apply reciprocal fees or visa requirements to US, Canadian and Australian nationals.

regions.name: Caribbean
regions.blurb: Caribbean islands are broadly visa-free for Western passports, and CARICOM nationals move freely between member states. Proof of accommodation and a return ticket are standard questions at immigration.

regions.name: Oceania
regions.blurb: Australia (ETA/eVisitor) and New Zealand (NZeTA) require electronic authorisation from nearly all visitors; Pacific island states are largely visa-free or visa-on-arrival.
